Nested calls run from the inside out, so you read `save(normalize(parse(read(file))))` backwards, counting parentheses on the way. Past a few levels, a variable with a good name for a step in the middle is easier to follow.

A call counts as nested when it is in an argument of another call or of a `new` expression. By default up to 3 levels are allowed, and each call that is deeper is reported.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 1} */}
```js
save(normalize(parse(read(file))));
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
const config = parse(read(file));
save(normalize(config));
```

A chain of methods is not nesting:

{/* good */}
```js
const total = text.trim().split(",").map(Number).filter(Boolean).reduce(add);
```

The count starts again inside a function, a class or JSX:

{/* good */}
```js
schedule(retry(withTimeout(() => save(normalize(config)))));
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max` | `3` | The deepest nesting that is allowed. |

{/* bad {"options": [{"max": 2}]} */}
```js
save(normalize(parse(text)));
```

{/* good {"options": [{"max": 4}]} */}
```js
save(normalize(parse(read(file))));
```
